items.title: Twisted Minds crowned as PGS 12 Champions
items.contents: [p][i]With PGS now firmly in the rear-view mirror, we sat down with PUBG expert and caster Jisooboy to get his take on Twisted Minds' dramatic win at PGS 12. Here's what he had to say:[/i][/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][i][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261110/w59OxLf4.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/i][/p][p align="start"]The king has returned.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] Twisted Minds was one of the most complete teams in the history of PUBG Esports. Living up to its reputation as a roster of world-class players, the team proved its abilities through results. Twisted Minds reached its peak between 2024 and 2025. In 2024, the team claimed three consecutive PGS titles. In 2025, it conquered the Esports World Cup (EWC), followed that victory with another championship at PGS 9, and finished as runners-up at PGS 10. Twisted Minds had established itself as a truly dominant force.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] The four players brought their individual strengths together and operated as one. BatulinS read the flow of every battlefield, xmpl initiated engagements, Perfect1ks kept pace with the evolving meta, and Lu stood as the team's unwavering last line of defense. Rather than relying on any single player's performance, all four understood their responsibilities and fulfilled their roles according to the situation. This was Twisted Minds' greatest weapon and the driving force behind its success.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] Twisted Minds was never simply a team that excelled at fighting. It knew when to engage, when to disengage, and when to begin applying pressure. From positioning and rotations that created favorable situations to the firepower needed to turn those advantages into victories, Twisted Minds possessed nearly everything required to succeed in PUBG.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]In 2026, PUBG Esports officially transitioned from FPP to TPP gameplay. This was far more than a change in camera perspective. Almost every aspect of competition evolved, from how teams gathered information and planned engagements to how they secured and defended positions.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] In FPP, players had to expose themselves to gain direct vision of their surroundings. In TPP, however, they could observe their surroundings from behind cover, and simply knowing an opponent's position could create a significant advantage. The ability to gather information safely, accumulate knowledge of the battlefield, and make rapid decisions became a competitive strength in its own right. These changes presented new challenges even for established powerhouses. Habits and decisions that had previously brought success could now become limitations under the new meta. Twisted Minds was no exception.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] In the past, Twisted Minds had excelled at reading the battlefield quickly and shaping matches according to its own plans. But in the new environment, those strengths no longer provided the same competitive edge. Its fighting ability also began to fall behind teams whose mechanical skills had improved dramatically. With both its rotations and engagements faltering, matches rarely unfolded as intended. The team often found itself struggling merely to reach and hold positions near the center of the circle. Other teams found it all too easy to exploit Twisted Minds when it was forced onto the defensive.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] Perhaps the weight of having won multiple international championships throughout 2024 and 2025 became a burden in itself. Adapting to a new environment required the team to question its established methods and, at times, abandon them entirely. But for a team that had already built such a refined system, changing those methods was never going to be easy. After all, those very methods had repeatedly delivered victories. To win again, Twisted Minds would have to aim even higher than the heights it had previously reached.[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261110/cFIxuQKb.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][p align="start"] The team's results in 2026 reflected these struggles. Twisted Minds failed to meet expectations from the opening stages of the PGS season, gradually drifting away from the center of the championship race after once dominating the global stage. There were moments of resurgence. The team finished third at PEC Spring 2026 and followed it with another third-place finish at PGS 4, briefly suggesting a return to form. But it could not sustain that momentum. At EWC 2026, where the stakes were especially high, Twisted Minds finished eighth and surrendered its defending champion status to the rising powerhouse Virtus.pro.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] What Twisted Minds needed was not simply to recover its previous form, but to develop a level of competitiveness that could once again succeed on the world stage. I kept watching to see how the team would overcome this difficult challenge. Yet considering its struggles in both fighting and macro play, I believed a comeback within 2026 was virtually impossible. One major reason was that xmpl, the team's primary fragger, and Lu, its last line of defense, were no longer performing at the level they once had.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"] The era when a single player could carry a team to an international championship was over. All four players needed to remain competitive individually for a team to have a realistic chance of winning. If even one or two failed to keep up, the entire team could quickly fall behind. Take Made in Thailand (MiTH), for example. Despite winning two PGS titles earlier this year and establishing itself as one of the strongest teams, MiTH had to compete with only three players at PGS 11 due to health issues and failed to reach the Final Stage. The consequences carried over into PGS 12, where MiTH slipped into the lower half of the standings.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Although Twisted Minds had not claimed a single championship before the final PGS Circuit concluded, I continued to watch the team closely, waiting to see if it could find a breakthrough.[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261110/riUik76q.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][p align="start"]First, BatulinS began making decisions much faster. The team became less inclined to push into the circle and simply hold its ground whenever circumstances turned unfavorable. Instead of trying to survive at all costs, it began actively intervening in other teams' engagements, committing its firepower to secure points. Even without a Chicken Dinner, the team could still earn points through its willingness to fight. BatulinS became noticeably more aggressive in engagements, and his success rate improved as well. Where he had previously excelled at identifying favorable positions and reading the overall situation, he now expanded the team's strategic options by directly taking down opponents.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Second, as the entire team shifted toward a more combat-oriented approach, xmpl began to rediscover his strengths as a fragger. When it comes to pure weapon handling, I can confidently say that only a handful of players in the world can match him. Professional players actually spend far less time shooting than one might imagine. Much of a match is devoted to looting, rotating, and scouting. Perhaps the increased frequency of engagements helped sharpen xmpl's instincts, because his statistics improved dramatically. He ranked first in kills (27), knocks (27), and average damage per match (391). His total damage reached an astonishing 5,871, putting him 1,611 ahead of second-place TGLTN (4,260). Most notably, he recorded 3,572 damage with DMRs, nearly five times his AR damage of 777, overwhelming countless opponents with his exceptional DMR firepower.[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261110/LxXhFlH9.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][p align="start"]Third, Perfect1ks demonstrated his ability to adapt to the new meta. Recently, he had begun making extensive use of buffed Light Machine Guns (LMGs). Even after certain aspects of their performance were adjusted in subsequent patches, he continued using them aggressively to destroy enemy vehicles. By eliminating opponents' means of transportation and restricting their mobility, he created opportunities to finish them off alongside xmpl. Mortars had not previously been a major part of the team's arsenal, but this time Perfect1ks took primary responsibility for using them and produced several decisive moments. In the PGS 12 Grand Finals, he recorded four mortar kills, ranking first in that category.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Finally, Lu, who had been trapped in a prolonged slump, made his return. Across countless tournaments, I had witnessed him dedicate himself to the team and rescue his teammates from seemingly hopeless situations. Even when the team faltered, Lu stood firm like a deeply rooted tree. But 2026 had been different. His shooting, decision-making, and remarkable clutch saves had all become noticeably less frequent. I had even argued that without Lu returning to form, there could be no resurgence for Twisted Minds in 2026. Yet in this tournament, Lu showed not only the player we remembered, but something even greater, playing a crucial role in the team's championship victory. With more precise utility usage and relentless survival instincts, he helped carry Twisted Minds back to the top.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261110/fbhxjdbz.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][p align="start"]Of course, the journey on the final day was far from smooth. On Day 3, Twisted Minds held the lead, but its challengers were closing in fast. In particular, eArena claimed a 10-kill Chicken Dinner in Match 11, firmly entering the championship race. DN SOOPers also refused to give up the chase. After Match 14, Twisted Minds stood at 119 points, while eArena had 117. Just two points separated them. With only one match remaining in the 15-match Grand Finals, the championship was still anyone's to claim.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Nevertheless, Twisted Minds did not waver. While its closest rivals gradually lost players, Twisted Minds maintained its strength and ultimately secured an 11-kill Chicken Dinner in the final match. Rather than simply waiting for its competitors to fall short, the team ended the tournament by taking matters into its own hands and decisively securing the title. With 140 points, Twisted Minds became the champion of the final PGS event of 2026.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Looking back, this championship was not simply a repeat of the glory Twisted Minds had enjoyed in 2025. Instead, it was the reward for a team that had been forced to leave its past successes behind, adapt to a new environment, and endure a long period of trial and error. Even for a team once regarded as the best in the world, the new era felt unfamiliar. Its trusted methods no longer worked as they once had, and the days when victory seemed almost inevitable were gone. But through those struggles, Twisted Minds discovered what it needed to change and rebuilt the level of performance required to reach the summit.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]When you sit upon the throne, it can be difficult to appreciate just how high you have climbed. Only after losing that place do you truly understand how difficult it is to rise again. Until last year, Twisted Minds occupied a position at the very top, one that no one could reasonably dispute. But in 2026, it surrendered that throne and endured a long period of uncertainty. After countless defeats and painful memories, the team finally reclaimed its crown at PGS 12. This time, it returned covered in scars, but stronger than ever.[/p][p align="start"]- Jisooboy[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261110/RtQfCfn7.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p]

items.title: PGS 12 Grand Finals Day 3 is LIVE!!
items.contents: [p]Hello, PUBG Esports fans![/p][p align="start"]The final stretch of the 2026 PUBG Global Series is approaching: [b]PGS Circuit 4[/b]. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and the Circuit Final, PGS 12, the three remaining tournaments will bring this year’s 12-event PUBG Global Series to a close.[/p][p align="start"]Circuit 4 is more than just the final circuit of the season. With the conclusion of PGS 12, the [b]final PGS Points standings for the 2026 season will be determined, deciding the eight teams that will advance to PUBG Global Championship 2026.[/b][/p][p align="start"]After three circuits of competition, the race for PGC is beginning to take shape—but nothing has been decided yet. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and double points on the line at PGS 12, there are still [b]240 PGS Points[/b] up for grabs.[/p][p align="start"]Which teams will earn their way to PGC 2026 through PGS Points? Let’s take a closer look at [b]Circuit 4, the final competition of the 2026 PGS season.[/b][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/QYvMFGPC.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS Circuit 4 Schedule[/b][/h2][p align="start"]PGS Circuit 4 will take place from [b]October 14 to November 1[/b].[/p][list][*][p][b]PGS 10[/b][/p][list][*][p]Group Stage: October 14[/p][/*][*][p]Winners Stage: October 15[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 16[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 17–18[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 11[/b][/p][list][*][p]Winners Stage: October 22[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 23[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 24–25[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 12[/b][/p][list][*][p]Survival Stage: October 29[/p][/*][*][p]Grand Finals: October 30–November 1[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p align="start"]As the [b]Circuit Final[/b], PGS 12 will see the top eight teams in the Circuit 4 PGS Points standings advance directly to the Grand Finals based on the points accumulated through PGS 10 and PGS 11. The remaining 16 teams will compete in the Survival Stage for the remaining spots in the Grand Finals.[/p][p align="start"]When PGS 12 comes to an end, it will mark not only the conclusion of Circuit 4, but also the end of the [b]2026 season-long PGS Points race spanning PGS 1 through PGS 12.[/b][/p][p align="start"][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/dfU4pJIb.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/b] [/p][h2][b]PGS Points Standings[/b][/h2][p align="start"]With three circuits and nine PGS events now complete, the battle for PGS Points is more intense than ever.[/p][p align="start"]At the conclusion of Circuit 3, [b]Virtus.pro leads the standings with 261 points[/b], followed by Made in Thailand with 224 points, 17Gaming with 223 points, and T1 with 208 points.[/p][p align="start"]Currently occupying the final PGC qualification spot is [b]Petrichor Road in eighth place with 152 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]But the gaps around the cutoff remain narrow. Seventh-place Falcons sit just two points ahead at 154, while ninth-place Gen.G Esports trail the current PGC qualification line by only seven points with 145.[/p][p align="start"]Most importantly, [b]Circuit 4 is still to come.[/b] The current standings are far from the final picture of who will advance to PGC.[/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/WQDtO1dg.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGC 2026 Qualification & PGS Points[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The [b]top eight teams in the final PGS Points standings[/b], accumulated across PGS 1 through PGS 12 during the 2026 season, will qualify for PGC 2026.[/p][p align="start"]And the final standings determine more than just qualification. The higher a team finishes in the PGS Points standings, the [b]later the stage from which they will begin their PGC 2026 journey.[/b][/p][p align="start"]The team finishing [b]1st in PGS Points will advance directly to the PGC 2026 Grand Finals[/b]. The [b]2nd-place team will enter at Survival Stage Day 1[/b], while the teams finishing [b]3rd through 8th will begin their journey in the Qualifying Stage[/b].[/p][p align="start"]This means Circuit 4 is about more than simply breaking into the Top 8. For teams already inside the qualification zone, the battle will continue until the very end as they fight for a higher PGS Points ranking and a more advantageous PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]240 PGS Points Are Still Up for Grabs[/b][/p][p align="start"]In both [b]PGS 10 and PGS 11[/b], the winner will earn [b]60 PGS Points[/b], with points awarded down through 16th place.[/p][p align="start"]At the Circuit Final, [b]PGS 12, the points will be doubled[/b]. The winner will earn 120 points, with 96 points going to second place, and double the PGS 10 and PGS 11 point values applied throughout the standings.[/p][p align="start"]That means the maximum number of points a single team can earn in Circuit 4 is:[/p][p align="start"][b]60 points (PGS 10 1st) + 60 points (PGS 11 1st) + 120 points (PGS 12 1st) = 240 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Considering the current gaps both inside and outside the PGC qualification zone, the three remaining tournaments leave plenty of room for the final standings to change.[/p][p align="start"]For teams outside the Top 8, Circuit 4 represents one final opportunity to make their move. For those already inside, it will be the final test to defend their position and secure a higher PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261012/lwSlSIQk.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS 10 Groups[/b][/h2][p align="start"]And it all begins with [b]PGS 10[/b].[/p][p align="start"]The Group Stage groups have been confirmed for the 24 teams competing in PGS 10. The teams have been divided into Groups A, B, and C through a [b]snake seeding format based on the final results of PGS 9.[/b][/p][p align="start"]PGS 9 winner Gen.G Esports has been placed in Group A, second-place T1 in Group B, and third-place Falcons in Group C. From there, the direction of placement alternates according to the PGS 9 standings, distributing all 24 teams across the three groups.[/p][list][*][p][b]Group A:[/b] Gen.G Esports, Made in Thailand, Virtus.pro, TEAM LIQUID, DN SOOPers, Sharper Esports, Team Vitality, Natus Vincere[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group B:[/b] T1, Alpha Gaming, Team Flash, eArena, Petrichor Road, FULL SENSE, TYLOO, JD Gaming[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group C:[/b] Falcons, Geekay Esports, Anyone’s Legend, 17Gaming, FOUR ANGRY MEN, Twisted Minds, 09(Team Nemesis at PGS 9), Godlike[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p align="start"][b]\[Updated: October 12][/b][/p][p align="start"]Following GAM The Expendables’ withdrawal from PGS Circuit 4, Team Flash has been selected as the replacement team based on its placement in PVS Phase 1, in accordance with the existing team qualification criteria.[/p][p align="start"][i]※ Further updates will be provided if there are any changes to the tournament.[/i][/p][/td][/tr][/table][/*][/list][h2][b]The Final Step to PGC[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The 2026 PUBG Global Series journey that began with PGS 1 now has just three tournaments remaining.[/p][p align="start"]There is still everything to play for after Circuit 3. With 60 points available at each of PGS 10 and PGS 11, followed by 120 points at PGS 12, [b]a total of 240 points remain on the table—and a single strong finish could reshape the race to PGC.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Which teams will finish inside the final Top 8 and earn their place at PGC 2026? And which team will rise to the very top of the standings to secure a direct seed to the [b]PGC Grand Finals[/b]?[/p][p align="start"]The final competition of the [b]2026 PUBG Global Series[/b] is about to begin.[/p][p align="start"][b]Tune in and cheer on your favorite teams as they make their final push toward PGC 2026![/b][/p]

items.title: 2027 PUBG Esports: What’s Changing
items.contents: [p]In 2027, PUBG Esports will introduce a new competitive structure.[/p][p]With updates to the existing regional competition system and the introduction of four Phases throughout the year, we aim to create a new competitive environment where more teams can compete for a place on the global stage and prove their skills.[/p][p]Take a closer look at the new competitive structure and key changes below.[/p][p][b]Regional Competition Updates[/b][/p][p]In 2027, PUBG Esports will introduce changes to its regional competition structure, including the division of existing regions and the addition of a new region.[/p][p]The existing [b]EMEA[/b] region will be divided into [b]Europe, Eurasia, and MENA[/b], while the [b]Americas[/b] will be divided into [b]North America and South America[/b]. [b]India, home to a massive community of PUBG fans and players, will join as a new competitive region[/b], creating more opportunities for teams to compete on the global stage.[/p][p]The race to qualify for PGS begins in each Regional League. Established teams and new challengers alike will compete at the regional level, with their results determining who advances to the global stage. With the updated regional competition structure, fans can look forward to new rivalries, new contenders, and more stories unfolding throughout the year.[/p][p][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261028/hpZM4KJD.png" style="border-style: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 0px 1px; user-select: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/b][/p][p][b]Four Phases, Four Chances[/b][/p][p]PUBG Esports in 2027 will feature four Phases, from Phase 1 through Phase 4.[/p][p]Each Phase consists of Regional Leagues and the corresponding PUBG Global Series (PGS).[/p][list][*][p][b]Phase 1[/b]: Regional League: Phase 1 → [b]PGS: Phase 1[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Phase 2[/b]: Regional League: Phase 2 → [b]PGS: Phase 2[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Phase 3[/b]: Regional League: Phase 3 → [b]PGS: Phase 3[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Phase 4[/b]: Regional League: Phase 4 → [b]PGS: Phase 4[/b][/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Each Phase brings a fresh opportunity to qualify for PGS, and securing a spot in one Phase does not guarantee participation in the next. [b]New challengers will have the chance to reach the global stage, while established teams must continue to prove themselves.[/b][/p][p]As part of this competitive restructuring, starting in 2027, [b]the Global Partner Team (GPT) program will evolve into a partnership focused on collaborative in-game items and marketing activities.[/b] All teams, including existing GPT teams, [b]will need to earn their place at PGS through their performance in each Phase’s Regional League, without guaranteed slots.[/b] Further details on the updated partnership will be shared in a future announcement.[/p][p][b]The next chance is earned through performance.[/b] Each of the four Phases brings a fresh challenge, creating new stories on the global stage.[/p][p][b]Introducing PUBG Esports Points[/b][/p][p]In 2027, [b]PUBG Esports Points[/b] will replace the existing points systems. Previously, PGC Points were awarded based on Regional League results, while PGS Points were awarded based on PGS results. Under the new system, [b]points will be awarded exclusively based on performance at PGS.[/b][/p][p]Teams will earn PUBG Esports Points based on their results at PGS. These points will accumulate throughout the year and count toward qualification for PGC. While the race from the Regional Leagues to PGS continues with each Phase, results achieved on the global stage will build throughout the year through PUBG Esports Points.[/p][p]Further details on the points distribution and PGC qualification system will be announced separately.[/p][p][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261028/yZdRyXdt.png" style="border-style: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 0px 1px; user-select: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/b][/p][p][b]2027 PUBG Esports Schedule[/b][/p][p]PUBG Esports in 2027 will begin with the Regional Leagues.[/p][p]Phase 1 and Phase 2 will take place in the first half of the year, followed by the 2027 PUBG Nations Cup in July. Phase 3 and Phase 4 will continue in the second half of the year, before the year concludes with the 2027 PUBG Global Championship.[/p][list][*][p][b]Phase 1[/b]: Late March – Early May[/p][/*][*][p][b]Phase 2[/b]: Mid May – Mid June[/p][/*][*][p][b]2027 PNC[/b]: Early July[/p][/*][*][p][b]Phase 3[/b]: Early August – Mid September[/p][/*][*][p][b]Phase 4[/b]: Late September – Early November[/p][/*][*][p][b]2027 PGC[/b]: Late November – Early December[/p][/*][/list][p]* The schedule above is subject to change.[/p][p]The changes coming in 2027 go beyond the competitive structure. Alongside the updated competition system, [b]a new look for PUBG Esports is also on the way. [/b]Stay tuned for more updates as PUBG Esports prepares for 2027.[/p][p]Further details on each Regional League’s schedule and format, PUBG Esports Points, and other tournament information will be shared in future updates.[/p][p]Thank you.[/p][p]PUBG Esports Team[/p]
